# ferriskey_portal_theme (Resource)

Manages a login portal theme (design tokens plus optional layout) in a FerrisKey realm. Page content is managed with `ferriskey_portal_theme_page` and activation with `ferriskey_portal_active_theme`. The API refuses to delete the currently active theme: destroying such a theme emits a warning and only removes it from Terraform state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ferriskey_portal_theme" "brand" {
  realm     = "acme"
  name      = "brand"
  layout_id = ferriskey_portal_layout.frame.layout_id

  config = jsonencode({
    colors = {
      primaryButton = "#0f766e"
      links         = "#0f766e"
    }
    spacing = {
      widgetPadding = 32
    }
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Theme name.
- `realm` (String) Name of the realm the theme belongs to. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `config` (String) Design tokens (`colors`, `fonts`, `borders`, `spacing`) as a JSON string, typically built with `jsonencode`. Omitted keys take server defaults; the server's defaults are not treated as drift as long as every configured key matches. When unset, the server-side config is exposed read-only. Note that the API replaces the whole config on every update.
- `layout_id` (String) UUID of the `ferriskey_portal_layout` framing the theme's pages; null for none.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite identifier `{realm}/{theme_id}`.
- `theme_id` (String) Server-assigned UUID of the theme.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import ferriskey_portal_theme.brand acme/4b2d7f90-1111-2222-3333-444455556666
```
